newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Interventions firm Mauritius rupee against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Interventions firm Mauritius rupee against dollar.

text.p: Market interventions by the central bank strengthened the Mauritius rupee's fixing against the dollar on Thursday, forex dealers said.
The rupee was quoted at a mean rate of 20.4265 for one dollar from 20.4595 on Wednesday. But against the pound, the rupee weakened to a mean rate of 33.344 from 32.966 Wednesday.

Dealers said the rupee firmed against the dollar as a result of central bank intervention on Wednesday early afternoon. It was the second market intervention this week as the central bank was also seen selling dollars to commercial banks on Monday.
"The central bank is sustaining the rupee. Interventions during the past couple of weeks were done at rates slightly below the prevailing interbank rate," one dealer said.
Last week, the central bank intervened three times, on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday.
With these market interventions, commercial banks were square in their foreign currency reserves, dealers said.

More hard currency inflow to commercial banks was expected on Thursday as the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate launched a morning tender sale of pounds obtained from sugar export, the Indian Ocean island's largest hard currency earner.
As from August 1996, the Syndicate can sell 25 percent of sugar export proceeds directly to banks while the remaining 75 percent is kept by the central bank for market interventions.
Forex dealers said the rupee was fixed weaker against the pound in line with trends in international markets.
